# BenderWu v1.0.6

This patch release fixes iterative buffer reuse and potential construction, checks BigFloat numeric contexts, and skips coefficients that vanish by symmetry. Public function signatures remain unchanged. Validation is stricter for invalid inputs, undersized buffers, and BigFloat context changes.

## Fixes

- `fill_Akl!` clears both buffers before filling them, so buffers can be reused across levels, potentials, and orders. Negative levels or orders and undersized buffers are rejected before any writes. [#12](https://github.com/schenkse/BenderWu.jl/pull/12)
- `Potential` promotes integer coefficients to floating point, with `Int` becoming `Float64` and `BigInt` becoming `BigFloat`. Fixed-width rational coefficients become `Rational{BigInt}`, including during accumulation of duplicate powers. The constructor copies its inputs and rejects nonfinite coefficients or a nonfinite harmonic frequency. Treat `pot.vcoeffs` as read-only. [#14](https://github.com/schenkse/BenderWu.jl/pull/14)
- A BigFloat potential is bound to the precision and rounding mode active at construction. `A_kl`, `ε_l`, and `fill_Akl!` throw `ArgumentError` when used under a different context. Construct a new potential inside the desired `setprecision` or `setrounding` context; `clear_cache!` does not change the binding. [#15](https://github.com/schenkse/BenderWu.jl/pull/15)

## Performance

- The iterative solver skips wave-function and energy coefficients that vanish by parity or by the greatest common divisor of the active perturbation indices. Skipped entries remain zero. [#16](https://github.com/schenkse/BenderWu.jl/pull/16)

## Documentation and benchmarks

- Corrected the explanation of perturbation orders for mixed potentials. `l` counts powers of `g` in `H(g) = -½∂ₓ² + V(gx)/g²`; a monomial `x^p` enters at `g^(p-2)`. Odd energy orders vanish for every potential. [#13](https://github.com/schenkse/BenderWu.jl/pull/13)
- Corrected the accuracy guidance for `find_epoly`. Recovering monomial coefficients is ill-conditioned at high order. Use rational arithmetic for exact coefficients, or choose BigFloat precision deliberately and compare results at higher precision. [#11](https://github.com/schenkse/BenderWu.jl/pull/11)
- Julia and Mathematica benchmarks now compare equivalent perturbation orders. Julia's maximum order `N` corresponds to the Mathematica package's order `N/2`, which counts powers of `g²`. [#17](https://github.com/schenkse/BenderWu.jl/pull/17)

[Full comparison with v1.0.5](https://github.com/schenkse/BenderWu.jl/compare/v1.0.5...v1.0.6)
